How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.
- `@Val` yields the same object the producer stored, **not a copy** — so an `Apply`
  step mutates the entity in place and later steps see the change.

### Naming

Verb plus entity: `Load<E>` (fetch by path variable, publishes `Out<E>`, throws when
absent) · `Build<E>` (construct from body) · `Validate<E>` (bind and validate the body,
publish it) · `Apply<E>` (mutate) · `Save<E>` · `Delete<E>` · `RespondWith<E>` (200) ·
`RespondWith<E>Created` (201) · `RespondWithNoContent` (204).

Keep DTOs at the edges — request body in at the first step, response DTO out at the
responder. Steps in between work with entities.

### Request body and validation

- The HTTP body can be read only once: **only one step per pipeline may bind
  `@RequestBody`**. A second binding fails at runtime. When later steps need it, the
  first step publishes it as a variable.
- `@Valid` runs before that step's method body, so step order decides when validation
  happens. Put the validating step first — otherwise a missing id returns 404 before an
  invalid body can return 400.

### Transactions

`govern: [ transaction ]` for writes, `govern: [ readonly-transaction ]` for reads,
listed on **every** step it covers. Both are provided by the starter. Governance spans
the pipeline, so the request commits once at the end.

### Errors

Functions throw; handlers respond. The exception must be **checked** (`extends
Exception`) so it appears in the `throws` clause. Put the handler in
`officefloor/escalation/<fully.qualified.ExceptionClass>.yml`, taking the exception as
`@Parameter` and responding via `ObjectResponse`. Matching is most-specific-first;
anything unmatched falls through to Spring `@RestControllerAdvice`.

### Security

Guard a whole endpoint file with a Spring Security SpEL expression:

```yaml
composition:
  authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"
```

=== period/PeriodCloser.java
/** Closes an open period, fixing its due-total as it is now (see ClosePeriod): used by a close by hand and by the
 *  automatic close a change of the sheet's today makes. */
=== period/AutoClosePeriods.java
/** Once the sheet's new today is stored, closes every open period (not closed nor soft-closed) whose to-date plus the sheet's grace days is before
 *  it (none while the grace days are blank), in order of their to-dates, exactly as a close by hand would, each
 *  writing PERIOD_CLOSED with auto=yes at its end. */
=== period/ClosePeriod.java
/** Closes an open period, fixing its due-total as it is now: the figures (each due as shown now, with its late charge)
 *  of the claims whose due-by falls in it and that counted by the status each had at the end of the period's last day,
 *  as its status log records it (a claim added after it does not count), the live rules otherwise applying (a
 *  person's claims OPEN or PENDING now and dated within a hold of theirs, not bound by a statement, do not, nor do deferred
 *  claims), added up (skipping n/a). Each person's own due-total for the period is fixed
 *  too, for every person on the sheet; the period's is the sum of theirs. Closing a period already closed is refused, and so is closing by a role the sheet's close permission does not allow. */
=== period/SoftClosePeriod.java
/** Soft-closes an open period: its due-total and each person's are fixed as a close fixes them (see ClosePeriod), but
 *  claims whose due-by falls inside it can still be added, edited, opened, settled and voided. Soft-closing a period closed or
 *  soft-closed already is refused, and so is soft-closing by a role the sheet's close permission does not allow. */
=== period/LockPeriod.java
/** Locks a period. Only a steward may lock it; locking a period that is already locked is refused. */
=== period/ReopenPeriod.java
/** Reopens a closed or soft-closed period, so its due-total is live again. Only a role the sheet's reopen permission allows (a steward while it is blank) may reopen; reopening a period that is
 *  not closed, or locked, is refused. */
=== period/PeriodRepository.java
/** The stored periods of each sheet. */
=== period/Period.java
/** A period of a sheet: a name unique on the sheet and its from and to dates, both inclusive. A closed period keeps
 *  the due-total fixed when it was closed; a soft-closed one ({@code soft}, not closed) keeps the due-total fixed when it
 *  was soft-closed, while claims whose due-by falls inside it can still change.
 *  {@code locked}: a steward locked it, so it cannot be reopened.
 *  {@code cap}, when set, is the most OPEN or PENDING claims a person may have in it (null: no cap). */
=== statement/TakeStatement.java
/**
 * Takes the person's statement on the sheet's today: their due-total now (the figures of their claims that count
 * added up, each with its late charge; n/a when their grade has no rate today and no counting claim has a
 * figure, kept or at the grade in force on its date; at most the sheet's cap), and binds every claim of theirs that counts (a person's OPEN or PENDING claims dated within a hold of theirs, or any once their retirement date is reached, not bound by a statement, do not, nor do deferred claims) to its due
 * as shown, its late charge (and the floor) included, so its late charge no longer follows today while bound (a claim
 * already bound keeps its bound figure); one that does not count is unbound (live again).
 *
 * Taken as of a date (on or before the sheet's today; a later one is refused, as is one before the person was added),
 * it is the same with the sheet as it stood at the end of that date (see SheetAsOf, PersonRepository#asOf): each claim
 * has the status its log shows then (one added later does not count), is bound only when the person's last statement
 * was taken while the sheet's today was on or before that date, and that date stands in for today in every figure.
 */
=== statement/CancelStatement.java
/**
 * Cancels the person's last statement: only a steward may, and a person with no statement is refused. The claims it
 * bound are unbound (live again); a figure an earlier statement bound is not restored.
 */
=== person/Person.java
/** A person on a sheet: a name (unique on the sheet, case ignored; kept without surrounding spaces) and a grade, one of A, B or C.
 *  The grade is dated: {@code grades} are the grades recorded, by from-date (the one with none, the first given, first), and
 *  {@code grade} is the one in force on the sheet's today.
 *  The version is 0 when added and goes up by one on each stored edit. {@code retiredFrom} (yyyy-MM-dd) is the date the
 *  person is retired from, null when not retired; a person with one counts as retired at once, whatever the date.
 *  {@code holds} are the person's holds, by from-date: an OPEN or PENDING claim of theirs dated within one, and not bound by
 *  a statement, counts in no live total. {@code held} is whether they have any hold. {@code terms} are the person's own
 *  terms (days a claim of theirs has until it is due by, ahead of their grade's and the sheet's) in force on the sheet's
 *  today, null when none; {@code ownTerms} are their own terms as recorded, by from-date (the one from the beginning of
 *  time, with none, first), a claim having those in force on its date. {@code contact} is the person's contact (unique on the sheet; kept without
 *  surrounding spaces, lower-cased), null when none. {@code aliases} are the person's aliases, sorted as names are compared
 *  (each kept without surrounding spaces; no alias equals, case ignored, any name or alias on the sheet). {@code clashing}
 *  is whether their name or an alias is used as a name or alias on another sheet of the sheet's tree (see
 *  PersonRepository#treeKeys): set only on the people listed, false elsewhere. {@code origin} is the sheet the person was
 *  last transferred from, null when they were never transferred here. {@code retirements} are the person's past
 *  retirements (each ended by unretiring them), in the order they ended. {@code tags} are the person's tags (each trimmed and
 *  in lower case, no repeats, sorted; empty when none): a claim of theirs counts for each in the tag totals. {@code flag} is the
 *  reason and until-date a steward last flagged them with, null when never flagged: while the sheet's today is on or before its
 *  until-date only a steward may open a claim of theirs (see PersonFlag). */
=== person/HoldPerson.java
/** Adds a hold on the person from the from-date (the sheet's today when blank) until the to-date, if any; a to-date
 *  before the from-date is refused. Publishes the hold as added (its from-date filled in). */
=== claim/ApplyClaimHold.java
/** Holds or releases the claim: only an OPEN or PENDING claim is. While held and not bound by a statement it counts in
 *  no live total, as a claim dated within a hold of its person does (see ClaimDue#countsLive). A claim already as asked
 *  is left as it is. */
=== person/AddImportedPeople.java
/** Stores the checked lines in the order pasted. A line matching a person updates them as the person form edits one:
 *  the grade recorded from the sheet's today (see ApplyPerson), the terms and contact set when the line gives them,
 *  written as PERSON_EDITED (see RecordPersonEdited). Any other adds a person as the form adds one, written as

Figures and the rules behind them ### Figures shown - **For a person:** `person-claimed`, `person-due-total`, `person-excess`, `person-settled-total`, `person-open-total`, `person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`, `person-period-

-due-total`, `person-period-

-carried`, `person-stated-total`, `person-cut-total` (pools), `person-terms`, `person-grade`, retired and hold status. - **For a claim:** `claim-number`, `claim-due`, `claim-due-by`, `claim-overdue`, `claim-status`, `claim-review-late`, `claim-stated`, `claim-corrects`, `claim-deferred` / `claim-deferred-until`, `claim-waived`, `claim-held`, `claim-proofs` (receipt and photo), `claim-late-entry`, `claim-batch`, `claim-period`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-reminded`. - **For the sheet:** rollup claimed, due, settled, open and overdue totals, classic, period, grade and tag totals. ### Which claims count (`ClaimDue.counts`, `countsLive`, `countsClaimed`; TS `counts`, `live`) - Only `OPEN`, `PENDING` and `SETTLED` claims count. - A **deferred** claim doesn't count: one that is `OPEN` with `deferredUntil` after the sheet's today. - **`retiredOut`** claims don't count: open, not bound by a statement, and the person's `retiredFrom` is on or before today. - **Claimed** adds up the amounts of the claims that count, leaving out corrections (claims with `corrects`). - `DRAFT`, `VOID`, `DELETED` and `REVIEW` claims count nowhere. ### How a claim's due is worked out (`ClaimDue.figure` → `LateCharge.add`; TS `claimDue`) 1. If `SETTLED`, the fixed `due`. 2. Else, if bound by a statement (`stated`), the `statedDue` as it is: no floor or late charge is added. 3. Else the **live** figure: amount × rate / 100, to 2 decimals. - The rate is for the person's grade on the claim's date (`gradeOn`), in force on that date. - If the sheet has no rate, it looks up through its parent sheets (`level`, at most 3) and then its clone/source chain. - A **forward-only rate** (`after` / `seqOf`) skips claims added before it was saved. - No rate gives n/a. 4. **Rounding** (`Rounding.mode`): - The dated `rounding` setting in force on `roundsOn` decides, if one is set. - Otherwise, before the `policy-date` (or today, if it's blank) rounds `HALF_UP`, and on or after it `HALF_EVEN`. - A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. 5. **Floor:** the figure is raised to at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). The overdue-total isn't capped. - **Sheet due-total and overdue-total:** drop the single highest and lowest person when 3 or more have one. The claimed-total, settled/open totals and the classic due sum aren't trimmed. - **Audit:** `ROLLUP`, `TOTALS` and `ALERT` lines are written when figures move. `ALERT` fires when a person's due-total crosses the `alert-threshold`. ### Due-by, numbering and dates - **`dueBy`** is fixed when the claim is added: the *terms*-th business day after its date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays (`HolidayRepository.businessDaysAfter`). - *Terms* are taken as they stand on the day it's added: the person's own terms, else `terms-`, else `terms` (default 14). - When a holiday is added, the due-by of every claim that isn't `SETTLED` or `VOID` and falls on or after it is worked out again (`refixDueBys`). - **A claim's date** defaults to the `entry-date` setting, else today. - **Number** (`ClaimNumbering`), given when a claim is opened: - `FY-n` by the fiscal year (`fiscal-start-month`) of its due-by, in one sequence shared across the sheet tree. - Once `period-numbering-from` is on or before today, `-n` instead, or `X-n` when no period holds its due-by. - A `REVIEW` claim gets no number until it is reviewed. - **Periods and closing** (all go by due-by): - A closed period refuses adding, editing, status changes, lock, defer, split, redate and reassign. - A soft-closed period freezes its totals but still allows changes; a claim added then is marked `lateEntry`. - Changing today auto-closes every period whose to-date plus `grace-days` is now past (`AutoClosePeriods`). - A locked period can't be reopened. - A period with a `cap` refuses opening a claim once the person has that many `OPEN`/`PENDING` claims in it (`overCap`). ### What gets frozen - **Settling** fixes `due`, with the late charge as of today (or as of a chosen date with settle-as-of, via `ClaimDueAsOf`). - **Re-settle** fixes it again at today's figure, ignoring any statement. - **`TakeStatement`** binds each claim that counts to its due as shown, late charge included. `CancelStatement` unbinds them. - **Closing or soft-closing a period** fixes the period's total and each person's period total and carried figure (claims due in earlier periods that were still open at the period's end, plus pasted openings). ### Who may do what - **Roles:** `clerk` (the default), `steward`, `viewer`. - A delegation makes a user act as steward while its dates include today. - Any change by a viewer, any change to an archived sheet, and any change from the as-of screen gets a 403 (`ViewerGuard`). - **`permits`:** open, settle, void and close default to clerk and steward; reassign and reopen to steward. Each can be overridden by `perm-*` settings. - **Four eyes:** the user who opened a claim, or last edited it, can't settle or approve it. - **Clerk limit:** a clerk settling above `clerk-limit-` (else `clerk-limit`, as in force today) makes the claim `PENDING`. Only a steward or the person's approver approves or rejects. - **Steward only:** voiding a `SETTLED` claim (within 7 days of settling), review, re-settle, waive, redate, flag, lock a period, cancel a statement. - **Flagged person:** only a steward opens their claims while the flag's until-date hasn't passed. - **Thresholds**, each taken on the claim's date: - Proof: settle and approve need a proof, and the configured proof kinds. - Note: a claim with no note can't be opened. - Review: opening sends the claim to `REVIEW` instead of `OPEN`. - **Void reasons:** required while the sheet has a list. - **Delete and restore:** a delete can only be restored on the same sheet-today. - **Corrections** (`Corrections`): a negative amount must name a `SETTLED` claim of the same person and can't exceed what remains of it. Refs are unique per sheet, ignoring case. - **Retirement:** a claim can't be dated after the retirement date or inside a past retirement (`mayClaimOn`), and a claim can't be reassigned to someone retired before its date. ### Imports and holds - **People import:** lines are `name,grade,terms,contact`. A line matching a person by name or alias edits them (the grade from today); any other line adds a person. It's all or nothing, and duplicates are refused. - **Paste claims:** adds `DRAFT` claims, or updates the matching `DRAFT`, then opens each line. All or nothing. - **Holds take nothing out of any total.** A person's hold only removes their pool cut while it covers today (`PoolRepository`), and a claim hold only shows `held`. ### Where the code and its own docs disagree These are worth knowing before you change anything: - **Holds:** the Javadoc on `Person`, `ApplyClaimHold`, `ClosePeriod` and `TakeStatement` says held claims count in no live total. The code (`countsLive`) ignores holds; the frontend and `Rollup` docs match the code. - **Retirement:** `Person` says a person "counts as retired at once, whatever the date". The code checks `retiredFrom` against today. - **Periods:** the TS `Period` doc says "dated inside"; the server checks due-by. - **Terms:** TS docs say a claim takes the terms in force "on its date"; the server uses the day it was added. - **Leftovers:** - `countsLive(claim, person)` ignores `person`, and `countsClaimed` is the same check as `countsLive`. In TS, `live` and `liveClaimed` are identical. - `ClaimRules.check` repeats `dueBy` inline instead of calling it, and `ApplyClaimStatus` and `ClaimDueAsOf` each have a private copy of `figure`. - The TS `total` adds amounts as floating-point numbers; everywhere else uses exact decimals. - **Rules in a migration:** due-by logic also lives in `V43__claim_due_by_business_days.java`. I traced the claim and person figures fully. I only read the top-level docs for pools, plans, crews, tags, aging and escalation. ## 2. How hard it was to follow Hard. The core formula is in about five small Java classes, but it is copied into a parallel TypeScript version. The rules about who may do what and when are spread across about 560 single-step pipeline classes and a dozen UI "slot" files. In several places the long prose comments contradict the code, so a new developer can't trust either copy alone.
